CREDITORS' CLAIMS AGAINST A DECEASED SETTLOR'S REVOCABLE TRUST (PROB. CODE § 19000 ET SEQ.; CODE CIV. PROC. § 366.2; ARLUK MEDICAL CENTER V. DOBLER; EMBREE V. EMBREE) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Alvin R. Embree · The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes what California law provides about the claims of a deceased settlor's creditors against the property of that settlor's revocable trust — the rule that property that was subject to the settlor's power of revocation at death remains answerable for the settlor's debts to the extent the probate estate is inadequate; what Part 8 of Division 9 of the Probate Code (sections 19000 through 19403) treats as a "claim"; the one-year outside limitations period that Code of Civil Procedure section 366.2 sets for an action on a liability of a person who has died; the fact that the trust claims procedure is optional and that no statute obliges a trustee to begin it; what changes for creditors and for trust beneficiaries when a trustee does begin it; the publication and known-creditor notice requirements; the deadline for filing a claim and the narrow route for a late claim; how a claim is filed and what it must contain; the trustee's allowance or rejection of a claim and the effect of silence; the 90-day period for an action on a rejected claim and the 120-day rule that protects later distributions; how money judgments against the deceased settlor or the trustee are paid; the personal liability of trust beneficiaries who received distributions when there was neither a probate proceeding nor a trust claims proceeding; and how a pending probate of the settlor's estate interacts with the trust claims procedure — as background in connection with The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014, of which Alvin R. Embree was the settlor and Dana R. Dobler is or was trustee, and the claim asserted or contemplated by Arluk Medical Center, in San Diego County, California. It states what the statutes and the published opinions say. It does not state whether any particular claim is timely, valid, or collectible, whether any procedure should be started, or what any person should do.

REVOCABLE TRUST PROPERTY REMAINS LIABLE FOR THE DECEASED SETTLOR'S DEBTS (PROB. CODE §§ 19001, 19002; ARLUK MEDICAL CENTER V. DOBLER)
Probate Code section 19001, subdivision (a), provides that upon the death of a settlor, the property of the deceased settlor that was subject to the power of revocation at the time of the settlor's death is subject to the claims of creditors of the deceased settlor's probate estate and to the expenses of administration of that probate estate, to the extent the probate estate is inadequate to satisfy those claims and expenses. Subdivision (b) allows a settlor, by appropriate direction in the trust instrument, to direct the priority of sources of payment of debts among subtrusts or other gifts established by the trust at death, but provides that no such direction alters the priority of payment of the matters set out in section 11420, which applies to the trust as it applies to a probate estate. Section 19002 states that, except as expressly provided, Part 8 is not to be construed to affect the right of any creditor to recover from any revocable trust established by the deceased settlor, and that nothing in Part 8 is a construction or alteration of the probate claims procedure in Part 4 (commencing with section 9000) of Division 7. In Arluk Medical Center Industrial Group, Inc. v. Dobler, the Court of Appeal described section 19001 in the same terms and, on the question before it, held that a trustee's only duty to such creditors is to refrain from affirmative misconduct that defeats the creditors' reasonable expectation of a recovery from trust assets; the court also stated that where the estate is inadequate to satisfy a judgment, the judgment creditor may proceed against the assets in the settlor's revocable living trust. Section 19001 speaks of property that was subject to the power of revocation at the settlor's death; The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014 is described in this sheet only as a trust of which Alvin R. Embree was the settlor, and this sheet does not determine what property, if any, was subject to a power of revocation held by Alvin R. Embree at death.

WHAT PART 8 TREATS AS A "CLAIM," AND WHAT IT DOES NOT (PROB. CODE § 19000)
Probate Code section 19000 defines the terms used in Part 8. Subdivision (a) defines a "claim" as a demand for payment for any of three listed things — whether due, not due, accrued or not accrued, or contingent, and whether liquidated or unliquidated: a liability of the deceased settlor, whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise; a liability for taxes incurred before the deceased settlor's death, whether assessed before or after that death, other than property taxes and assessments secured by real property liens; and a liability for the funeral expenses of the deceased settlor. Subdivision (b) provides that a "claim" does not include a dispute regarding title to specific property alleged to be included in the trust estate. Subdivision (c) defines a "creditor" as a person who may have a claim against the trust property. Subdivision (d) defines the "trust" for this purpose as a trust described in section 18200 or, if a portion of a trust, that portion that remained subject to the power of revocation at the deceased settlor's death, and subdivision (e) defines a "deceased settlor" as a deceased person who at the time of death held the power to revoke the trust in whole or in part. Subdivision (h) defines the "trust estate" as a decedent's real and personal property that is titled in the name of the trustee of the deceased settlor's trust or confirmed by order of the court to that trustee. Section 19012 provides that Part 8 applies to claims against any deceased settlor who dies on or after January 1, 1992, and that the law in effect before that date continues to apply to claims against a settlor who died earlier. Whether a demand asserted by Arluk Medical Center is a "claim" within these definitions, and whether The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014 or any part of it was subject to a power of revocation held by Alvin R. Embree, are questions this sheet does not answer.

THE ONE-YEAR OUTSIDE LIMIT ON AN ACTION ON A DECEASED PERSON'S LIABILITY (CODE CIV. PROC. § 366.2)
Code of Civil Procedure section 366.2, subdivision (a), provides that if a person against whom an action may be brought on a liability of the person — whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise, and whether accrued or not accrued — dies before the expiration of the applicable limitations period, and the cause of action survives, an action may be commenced within one year after the date of death, and the limitations period that would have been applicable does not apply. Subdivision (b) provides that this one-year period is not to be tolled or extended for any reason except as provided in four listed places, which include Code of Civil Procedure sections 12, 12a, and 12b, the probate creditor-claim provisions in Part 4 (commencing with section 9000) of Division 7 of the Probate Code, and Part 8 (commencing with section 19000) of Division 9 of the Probate Code — the trust claims part this sheet describes. Subdivision (c) applies the section to actions brought on liabilities of persons dying on or after January 1, 1993. Two sections of Part 8 repeat the point from the Probate Code side: section 19100, subdivision (c), states that the claim-filing period is not to be interpreted to extend or toll any other statute of limitations, including section 366.2, and section 19103, subdivision (b), states that nothing in it authorizes allowance or approval of a claim barred by, or extends the time provided in, section 366.2. In Embree v. Embree the Court of Appeal applied that structure to a judgment creditor who sued the beneficiaries of a deceased judgment debtor's revocable living trust more than a year after the death. How section 366.2 applies to any demand by Arluk Medical Center arising out of a liability of Alvin R. Embree is a question this sheet does not answer.

THE TRUST CLAIMS PROCEDURE IS OPTIONAL, AND NO STATUTE REQUIRES A TRUSTEE TO BEGIN IT (PROB. CODE §§ 19003, 19008, 19010; ARLUK MEDICAL CENTER V. DOBLER)
Probate Code section 19003, subdivision (a), provides that at any time following the death of the settlor, and during the time that there has been no filing of a petition to administer the probate estate of the deceased settlor in this state of which the trustee has actual knowledge, the trustee may file with the court a proposed notice to creditors; upon the court's assignment of a proceeding number to that proposed notice, the trustee is then to publish and serve notice to creditors in the form and within the time prescribed in Chapters 3 and 4 of Part 8, and that action constitutes notice to creditors of the requirements of the part. Subdivision (b) directs where the filing is made: the superior court for the county in this state where the deceased settlor resided at death, or if none, any county in this state in which trust property was located at the settlor's death, or if none, the county that was the principal place of administration of the trust at that time. Section 19010 states that nothing in Part 8 imposes any duty on the trustee to initiate the notice proceeding set out in section 19003, and that the trustee is not liable for failure to initiate the proceeding. Section 19008 states the consequence of not beginning it: if there is no proceeding to administer the probate estate and the trustee neither files a proposed notice to creditors nor publishes notice, the liability of the trust to any creditor of the deceased settlor is as otherwise provided by law. In Arluk Medical Center Industrial Group, Inc. v. Dobler the Court of Appeal described the procedure as entirely optional and stated that a trustee incurs no liability for deciding to forgo it and distribute trust assets. Whether Dana R. Dobler has begun or may begin such a proceeding as to The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014 in San Diego County is not a question this sheet answers.

WHAT CHANGES WHEN THE TRUSTEE DOES BEGIN THE PROCEDURE (PROB. CODE §§ 19004, 19006; ARLUK MEDICAL CENTER V. DOBLER)
Probate Code section 19004 states the consequences that follow if the trustee files, publishes, and serves notice as set out in section 19003: all claims against the trust must then be filed in the manner and within the time provided in Part 8; a claim that is not so filed is barred from collection from trust assets; and the holder of a claim may not maintain an action on the claim against the trust unless the claim is first filed as Part 8 provides. Section 19006, subdivision (a), extends the protection: if a trustee of a trust established by the deceased settlor files, publishes, and serves the notice, the protection from creditors afforded that trustee and trust is also afforded to any other trusts established by the deceased settlor and to the trustees and beneficiaries of those trusts. Subdivision (c) gives the trustee a right of collection against a probate estate later opened, to recover the amount of any debts paid from trust assets that would otherwise have been satisfied by the property subject to the probate proceedings. In Arluk Medical Center Industrial Group, Inc. v. Dobler the Court of Appeal summarized the same point, stating that if the trustee properly utilizes the optional procedure, property distributed from the trust is no longer subject to creditors' claims. Whether notice has been given as section 19003 requires in connection with The Embree Family Revocable Trust dated March 4, 2014, and what effect that would have on any demand by Arluk Medical Center, are questions this sheet does not answer.

NOTICE TO CREDITORS: PUBLICATION AND NOTICE TO KNOWN CREDITORS (PROB. CODE §§ 19040, 19050)
Probate Code section 19040, subdivision (a), requires that publication of notice be for at least 15 days, and provides that three publications in a newspaper published once a week or more often, with at least five days intervening between the first and last publication dates (not counting the first and last publication dates as part of the five-day period), are sufficient. The subdivision directs where the notice is published — a newspaper of general circulation in the city, county, or city and county where the deceased settlor resided at death, or if none, where trust property was located at the settlor's death, or if none, where the principal place of administration of the trust was located — with fallbacks to the nearest such newspaper circulated in the area and, if there is no such newspaper, to posting in three of the most public places in the community. Probate Code section 19001, subdivision (a), provides that upon the death of a settlor, the property of the deceased settlor that was subject to the power of revocation at the time of the settlor's death is subject to the claims of creditors of the deceased settlor's probate estate and to the expenses of administration of that probate estate, to the extent the probate estate is inadequate to satisfy those claims and expenses. expectedJSON.body: Probate Code section 19000 defines the terms used in Part 8. Subdivision (a) defines a "claim" as a demand for payment for any of three listed things — whether due, not due, accrued or not accrued, or contingent, and whether liquidated or unliquidated: a liability of the deceased settlor, whether arising in contract, tort, or otherwise; a liability for taxes incurred before the deceased settlor's death, whether assessed before or after that death, other than property taxes and assessments secured by real property liens; and a liability for the funeral expenses of the deceased settlor. Subdivision (b) provides that a "claim" does not include a dispute regarding title to specific property alleged to be included in the trust estate. Subdivision (c) defines a "creditor" as a person who may have a claim against the trust property. Subdivision (d) defines the "trust" for this purpose as a trust described in section 18200 or, if a portion of a trust, that portion that remained subject to the power of revocation at the deceased settlor's death, and subdivision (e) defines a "deceased settlor" as a deceased person who at the time of death held the power to revoke the trust in whole or in part. Subdivision (h) defines the "trust estate" as a decedent's real and personal property that is titled in the name of the trustee of the deceased settlor's trust or confirmed by order of the court to that trustee. Section 19012 provides that Part 8 applies to claims against any deceased settlor who dies on or after January 1, 1992, and that the law in effect before that date continues to apply to claims against a settlor who died earlier. Embree, are questions this sheet does not answer.

expectedJSON.body: Probate Code section 19003, subdivision (a), permits a trustee to file a proposed notice to creditors only during the time that there has been no filing of a petition to administer the probate estate of the deceased settlor in this state of which the trustee has actual knowledge. Section 19006, subdivision (b), supplies the counterpart: if the personal representative of the deceased settlor's probate estate has published notice under section 8120 and given notice of administration under Chapter 2 (commencing with section 9050) of Part 4 of Division 7, the protection from creditors afforded that personal representative is afforded to the trustee and to the beneficiaries of the trust. Subdivision (c) of the same section gives the trustee, where a probate proceeding requiring publication under section 8120 is later commenced, a right of collection against that probate estate for debts paid from trust assets that would otherwise have been satisfied out of the probate property. In Arluk Medical Center Industrial Group, Inc. v. Dobler the Court of Appeal described this arrangement, stating that a trustee with actual knowledge of instituted probate proceedings is statutorily barred from initiating a trust claims procedure, and that in that situation the notice of probate proceedings constitutes sufficient notice to all claimants that they must file a timely claim in the probate proceedings or be barred from later asserting the claim against either the estate or the trust. Whether a petition to administer the probate estate of Alvin R. Embree has been filed in San Diego County or elsewhere, and what follows from that for Dana R. Dobler or Arluk Medical Center, are questions this sheet does not answer.
